title: What Ironworking Is All About
description: Ironworkers erect structural steel for buildings and bridges, install reinforcing steel in concrete, and handle ornamental metalwork. They work at height with cranes, welding, and rigging to raise the skeletons of structures. High-rise construction, bridge projects, industrial plants, and stadiums. Structural, reinforcing, and ornamental specialties each have their own crews and rhythms. This record lays the foundation: the core purpose, the people it serves, and where it fits in everyday life.

title: History and Evolution
description: Ironworkers raised America's skylines: the trade organized in 1896 and built the skyscraper age, from the Empire State Building to modern towers. Mohawk ironworkers became legendary high-steel crews. Safety advances replaced the daredevil era with engineered fall protection. Knowing where the trade came from explains why things are done the way they are — and which 'rules' are just old habits.

Let beginners struggle productively.
Mentor one person to start.
how_it_works: Offer to show a beginner the basics.
Prepare a simple lesson plan.
Demonstrate, then watch and coach.
Ask what confused them and improve.
